The Pskov eparchy and its major monasteries underwent notable administrative reshuffling right around 1730–1731. Feofan is strongly associated with the governance and oversight of the Pskov monastic institutions during these exact years, appearing frequently in archival records tied to the Pskov-Caves (Pskovo-Pechersky) Monastery at that time.

Because of how short this tenure was, 18th-century synodal chronicles sometimes conflate the exact dates of the monastery's leadership during the late 1720s and early 1730s, but the formal appointment for 1730–1731 belongs to Markell.

Therefore, my initial vote is **F**.
